name: VoltLine MicroTaser MT-2 'Bite'
description:
A compact contact stun device the size of a cigarette lighter, delivering a 50,000-volt low-amperage electrical discharge through two prong electrodes on the business end. The MT-2 is the most basic stun device available in GLMZ — press it against an attacker, press the button, and the electrical discharge causes involuntary muscle contraction and immediate pain. The low amperage means it is unlikely to cause cardiac events in healthy individuals, though VoltLine's documentation includes the standard disclaimers about pre-existing conditions.

VoltLine manufactures the MT-2 in a facility in Tier 2 using largely automated production, keeping costs low enough that the device retails for Φ35. It recharges via standard micro-cell, and a full charge provides approximately thirty discharges. The device is available in a range of colors and finishes, from utilitarian black to bright patterns — VoltLine recognized early that self-defense devices that people actually carry need to not look like weapons.

The MT-2's limitation is that it requires direct physical contact — the user must be within arm's reach of the attacker and must press the electrodes against skin or thin clothing. This means the user is already in danger when the device becomes useful, which critics argue makes it a reactionary tool rather than a preventive one. VoltLine's response is that most street attacks begin at close range, and having any deterrent at contact distance is better than having none.
specifications:
voltage: 50,000V
amperage: 3.6 milliamps (non-lethal threshold)
electrode gap: 1.2 cm
discharges per charge: 30
recharge time: 45 minutes from depleted
weight: 38 g
dimensions: 7 cm x 3 cm x 1.5 cm
cost: Φ35
tactical_use: Press electrodes firmly against attacker's exposed skin or thin clothing and hold the button for at least one second. Optimal target areas are the neck, armpit, and inner thigh where nerve density is highest. The discharge causes involuntary muscle contraction and pain but does not reliably incapacitate — treat it as a distraction tool that creates a one-to-two-second window to break away. Ineffective through thick clothing, armor, or dermal augmentations.
cultural_context: The MT-2 is carried by millions of GLMZ residents who want something more than an alarm but can't afford or don't want to carry chemical sprays. Its lighter-like form factor means it disappears into a pocket or bag without bulk. VoltLine's marketing is matter-of-fact — no tough-guy imagery, no fear-based messaging, just the simple proposition that Φ35 buys you a chance to get away. The device has become so common that muggers have adapted, wearing thicker clothing and gloves specifically to defeat contact stun devices.
story_hooks: A modified MT-2 with boosted amperage has been linked to a cardiac arrest death in Tier 1 — the modification is a simple capacitor swap that any electronics hobbyist could perform.

VoltLine's manufacturing facility has been producing devices with inconsistent voltage output — some units barely function while others deliver dangerous overcharges, suggesting sabotage on the production line.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, pocket-sized stun device with the form factor of a premium lighter or compact vape — deliberately non-threatening industrial design. Rounded edges with a subtle ergonomic grip, dual prong electrodes protruding from one end like small fangs.
physical_description.dimensions: 70 mm length × 30 mm width × 15 mm depth. Electrode protrusion: 12 mm
physical_description.weight_description: Feather-light in hand — 38 grams gives it almost no heft, making it feel more like a utility gadget than a weapon. Balanced enough for single-hand operation despite the compact size.
physical_description.primary_material: Injection-molded thermoplastic polymer body with hardened steel electrode prongs. Internal capacitor housing visible as subtle ribbed reinforcement along seams.
physical_description.finish: Matte or satin polymeric coating with subtle texture for grip. VoltLine offers utilitarian black as standard, but also bright neon accents (electric blue, safety orange, hot pink) on grip areas and button housing to read as civilian tech rather than weaponry.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary matte black or dark grey polymer; accent colors on thumb button and grip strip (often high-visibility or aesthetic brights). Electrode prongs: brushed steel or gunmetal grey.
physical_description.grip_texture: Subtly textured thermoplastic with micro-grip pattern — slightly adhesive feel that prevents slip even in wet conditions. Thumb button area molded with slight finger notch for intuitive control.
distinctive_features: Dual steel electrode prongs separated by 12 mm gap, slightly splayed for contact consistency
Low-profile power button on top edge, recessed slightly to prevent accidental discharge
Micro-cell charging port (proprietary connector) on rear lower edge
Subtle indicator LED on button housing — green when charged, amber when depleted
Safety lever or physical contact guard (optional variant) that must be cleared before discharge
Minimalist VoltLine branding: small embossed logo on grip panel
Serial number plate (2 mm × 8 mm) stamped on rear lower body
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: VoltLine Personal Electronics logo (small, understated) embossed on grip side. Model designation 'MT-2' printed in tiny text near charging port. Serial number stamped on rear. No aggressive branding — deliberately manufactured to read as consumer electronics.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine or lightly used — designed for high-volume consumer market so most examples are well-maintained. Worn units show minor scuffing on edges and slight discoloration around button from repeated thumb contact. Battery indicator may show age (amber more frequently). No rust or corrosion due to polymer-dominated construction.
